contexts.WH: "......I did think of it that way.  Anyway, as soon as I became aware, I was living like that.  I didn't even think to question it."
contexts.MG:
"......What do you mean by that?
...Are you trying to say that, as far back as you can remember, you were always a bird in a cage?"

I didn't even think to question it."

"...............What do you mean by that?

findings.sourceReading: She thought this was simply how things were, since it had been her life from earliest awareness and she never questioned it.
findings.alternative: The next sentences preserve her lack of questioning, but the opening reply refers to taking the situation for granted, not adopting a metaphor of confinement.

外へ出たいと、きっと生まれて初めてに違いない決意を、口にしたのだ。

contexts.WH: She put that resolution to go outside into words, that resolution which she had surely been born with.
contexts.MG:
And despite that, she had made her decision.
She'd voiced her decision to go outside, a decision she was probably making for the first time in her life.
contexts.UP:
And she had taken that into consideration, and resolved herself.
She had put that resolution to go outside into words, for what was surely the first time in her entire life.
contexts.note: Both editions correctly present this as probably Beatrice’s first such decision in her life, rather than a resolution possessed from birth.

findings.sourceReading: She voices a decision to go outside that she has probably made for the first time in her life.
findings.alternative: 生まれて初めて is the ordinary expression for first time in one’s life; it does not mean possessed since birth.

findings.description: WH calls the soft smile farsightedness instead of a composed or detached understanding reached after resolving to depart.

contexts.japanese:
彼女が、ようやく、とてもやわらかい笑顔を見せてくれたので、ちょっぴりだけ驚いてしまった。
それはひょっとすると、
…篭より旅立つ覚悟ができたからこその、達観なのか。
それまでの暗い顔からは想像もつかないくらい、やわらかい笑顔だった…。
contexts.japanesePC: それはひょっとすると、…篭より旅立つ覚悟ができたからこその、達観なのか。

それまでの暗い顔からは想像もつかないくらい、やわらかい笑顔だった…。
contexts.WH: Could that have been, ...a farsightedness caused by her determination to venture out from her cage?
contexts.MG:
I was just a little surprised when she finally gave me a gentle smile.
Could that have been...
a farsightedness brought about by her decision to venture out from her cage?
It was a smile so gentle, I couldn't imagine that it had come from that once dark face...
contexts.UP:
I was just a little surprised when she finally showed me a very soft smile.
That might have been...
an inner peace, coming from her newfound readiness to venture out from her cage.
A soft smile which I wouldn't have imagined could have come out of that dark face...
contexts.note: MG retains “farsightedness.” UP renders 達観 as inner peace arising from her readiness to leave, preserving the composed emotional state.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa wonders whether her smile reflects the serenity of having made up her mind to leave the cage.
findings.alternative: 達観 can involve a broad view, but farsightedness emphasizes future anticipation rather than the emotional composure contrasted with her previous dark expression.

contexts.note: Both editions describe Rosa as growing impatient, retaining WH’s emotional shift from anxious or flustered urgency.

findings.sourceReading: She becomes anxious or flustered at the prospect of being caught in the forest after dark.
findings.alternative: 焦る can include impatience, but the explicit impending danger and being lost indicate anxious urgency rather than frustration at waiting.

だって、後についてくる彼女はこんなにも無邪気で楽しそう。
…だからこそ、私は彼女の笑顔のためにも、
絶対にこの森の外へ案内してあげなければならないのだ。

contexts.WH: But there was no reason to complain.
contexts.MG:
At this rate, night would definitely fall before I had a clue where to walk.

contexts.note: MG uses “no time to cry” and UP “didn’t have the luxury to complain”; both preserve inability to indulge distress while responsible for Beatrice.

findings.sourceReading: She cannot sit there whining; she must guide the trusting woman out.
findings.alternative: No reason could idiomatically discourage complaining, but the source leaves her genuine distress intact and focuses on the obligation to act despite it.

findings.description: WH says Rosa thought there was no other way, replacing her consideration of whether there was another plan because the proposed descent looked dangerous.

contexts.japanese:
私はずっと森の中を歩いていて疲れていたから、
たとえ岩浜であっても、開けた場所の方がずっと歩きやすいだろうと考えた。
だから、何とかして岩壁を降りようと提案したの。
…一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。
でも、ベアトリーチェは私の提案に何の疑いもなく頷いた。
contexts.japanesePC: …一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。
contexts.japanesePS3:
私はずっと森の中を歩いていて疲れていたから、

でも、ベアトリーチェは私の提案に何の疑いもなく頷いた。
contexts.WH: ...It looked pretty dangerous, but I thought there was no other way.
contexts.MG:
I was tired from walking around the forest for so long,
so I figured that an open area, even a rocky beach, would probably be much easier to walk in.
So, I suggested that we go down that rocky cliff somehow.
...It looked pretty dangerous, but I figured there was no other way.
However, Beatrice agreed to my plan without any doubts.
contexts.UP:
I was tired from walking around the forest for so long,
so I thought that even though it was a rocky beach, an open area would probably be much easier to walk in.
So I planned to somehow go down the rocky cliff.
...It did look pretty dangerous, and I wondered if there was some other way.
However, Beatrice agreed with my plan without any doubts.
contexts.note: MG retains the conclusion that there was no other way. UP restores Rosa’s open question about whether another route exists.

findings.sourceReading: She proposes descending but, because it looks dangerous, wonders whether another plan is possible.
findings.alternative: An implicit request for alternatives may reflect limited options, but 他に案はないか is an open question; WH supplies the negative conclusion before Beatrice agrees.

contexts.WH: Don't mess with me, that can't be...!  Rosa oba-san was a kid, so she was rushed.  It's not like there was a doctor.  She probably made a mistake, thinking you were dead, and you probably, umm, ......were alive and pretending to be dead or something.  Isn't that right?!"

"Don't mess with me, that's impossible...!

And it's not like a doctor was there.
She probably just mistakenly thought you were dead, and you were probably...umm...alive and pretending to be dead or something.
Isn't that right?!"
It can't be true.
She's got to be alive.
Otherwise, how can she be here...?!
...The kid-aged Aunt Rosa shook Beatrice's body, crying.
I stared into that face too,
......but her eyes were still open, and it really was a corpse.
...I wanted to dodge the issue by saying something vague, like "she must be playing dead",
...but no matter how I looked at it, it didn't look fake at all, ...it really did look like she was dead...
contexts.UP:
"Don't mess with me, that can't be...!
Auntie Rosa was a kid, and she was panicking.
It's not like there was a doctor.
She probably made a mistake, thinking you were dead, and you probably, umm, ......were in a state of apparent death, or something, but actually alive.
Right?!"
It can't be.
She's obviously alive.
Otherwise, she wouldn't be here in front of me, right...?!
...The kid‐aged Auntie Rosa was shaking Beatrice's body, crying.

contexts.note: MG retains voluntary pretending or playing dead. UP consistently restores a state of apparent death without deliberate performance.

findings.sourceReading: He proposes she was alive in a state of apparent death or something similar and that Rosa mistakenly judged her dead.
findings.alternative: The wider dispute may permit a feigned-death theory, but 仮死状態 identifies a deathlike living condition, not an act of pretending; no doctor and Rosa’s panic support misdiagnosis.

そして金蔵によって呼び出され、長い時間、囚われの身であったことを思い出す…。
肉の檻に囚われている間、妾の魔女としての記憶は完全に失われていた。
しかし、楼座のお陰で、とでも言うべきか。
事故で死ねたお陰で、妾は今、ようやく自らを取り戻したのだ……。
「……楼座。
そなたは妾を死なせてしまったと後悔しているだろうが。
妾にとっては感謝したいくらいよ。
くっくっくっく…！」
contexts.WH: Thanks to my accidental death, I had now finally brought myself together......
contexts.MG:
Eventually, I felt the memory returning...
The fact that I was an Endless Witch who had lived for one thousand years.
Then, I remembered that I'd been summoned by Kinzo, and that I'd been imprisoned by him for a long time...
While being imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I completely lost my memory as a witch.
However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that...
...Thanks to my accidental death, I'd now finally regained my self...
"...Rosa,
you probably regret bringing about my death.
But I should be thanking you.
*cackle*cackle*...!"
contexts.UP:
Eventually, I felt the memory returning...
The fact that I was an Endless Witch who had lived for one thousand years.
And then I remembered that I had been summoned by Kinzo, and for a long time, had been imprisoned by him...
While I had been imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I had completely lost my memory as a witch.
However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that...
Thanks to my accidental but fortunate death, I had now finally brought myself together......
"......Rosa.
You are probably regretting that you brought about my death.
But as for me, I could even thank you.
*cackle*cackle*...!"
contexts.note: MG restores that Beatrice regained herself. UP retains “brought myself together,” suggesting composure rather than recovered identity.

findings.sourceReading: Through being able to die accidentally, she has finally regained herself, including her witch memories and identity.
findings.alternative: Bringing oneself together can suggest composure or consolidation, but the preceding restored memories and cage-induced loss establish recovering identity, not merely emotional composure.

contexts.WH: That should suit you, let's do that.  I now thoroughly know of your unskillful method of attack!  *cackle*cackle*cackle* hihihihihihihihihihi!!"

"They say you should play the opening like a book, the middle game like a magician,
and the endgame like a machine.
I'll corner you from here on.
Slowly, carefully, ...surely.
Or, on the other hand, would it be better if I pressed you all at once, which might suit your style more?"
"Yes, that should fit you well, let's do that.
I'm now fully aware of the sorts of attacks you're weakest against!
*cackle*cackle*cackle* Hihihihihihihihihihi!!"

and the endgame like a machine.

findings.sourceReading: She knows exactly what kind of attack he has trouble facing.
findings.alternative: 苦手 can describe poor performance, but the preceding promise to press him establishes her attack on him, not his attack on her.

findings.description: The formal game formula 復唱要求 means “repetition requested.” Repeat it replaces the stable procedural label with an ordinary direct command.

findings.description: 今日まで says that no one has answered Beatrice's question to this day, including the present. Until today can imply that the situation changed today and someone has now answered it.

……なぜか皆、目を逸らし、はぐらかす」

"...Who am I?

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice says that no one has ever answered who she is through the present moment; everyone still averts their gaze and evades her.
findings.alternative: Until today is often used loosely to include the present day, and the immediately following evasion makes clear that no answer has just arrived.

findings.description: この疑問を…抱かせないため says Kinzo's behavior seems intended to prevent Beatrice from continuing to harbor this doubt. Force me to stop my further questioning changes the internal uncertainty into overtly asking questions.

…しかし、その仕草もまた、妾にこの疑問をこれ以上、抱かせないためのものにしか感じられない。
「………………………。
…ふ。
……やはり、…そなたもそれを語ってはくれぬのか」
contexts.japanesePC: …しかし、その仕草もまた、妾にこの疑問をこれ以上、抱かせないためのものにしか感じられない。

contexts.WH: ...However, I couldn't help but feel that this behavior was another attempt to force me to stop my further questioning.
contexts.MG:

"............

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice reads Kinzo's dismissive laugh as another attempt to keep her from dwelling further on the unresolved question of her identity.
findings.alternative: Her internal doubt has already led her to question Kinzo directly, so stopping further questioning can stand metonymically for suppressing the doubt.

findings.alternative: His hypothetical requires revival after Rosa can no longer observe it, and immediate revival is one possible version, but the source supplies no “as soon as” constraint.

findings.description: UP renders 消極的な自殺 as “half-hearted suicide.” The phrase means passive suicide: disappearing and exposing oneself to harm without directly performing a decisive suicidal act. “Half-hearted” instead suggests weak commitment or insufficient resolve.

でも、とにかくお屋敷と今の自分から逃げ出したかった。
……ある意味それは、家出でもあり、消極的な自殺でもあった…。
「……いなくなりたかったの。
…あるいは、いなくなることによって親を心配させたいという、子どもなりの反抗だったのかも…」

findings.alternative: Rosa’s intent is ambivalent, so “half-hearted” can convey that she did not fully or directly commit to dying.

だから、何とかして岩壁を降りようと提案したの。
…一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。
でも、ベアトリーチェは私の提案に何の疑いもなく頷いた。

contexts.MG:
I was tired from walking around the forest for so long,
so I figured that an open area, even a rocky beach, would probably be much easier to walk in.
So, I suggested that we go down that rocky cliff somehow.
...It looked pretty dangerous, but I figured there was no other way.
However, Beatrice agreed to my plan without any doubts.
contexts.UP:
I was tired from walking around the forest for so long,
so I thought that even though it was a rocky beach, an open area would probably be much easier to walk in.
So I planned to somehow go down the rocky cliff.
...It did look pretty dangerous, and I wondered if there was some other way.
However, Beatrice agreed with my plan without any doubts.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa proposes that they somehow descend the rocky cliff, while also wondering whether another plan might be possible because it looks dangerous.
findings.alternative: A plan can be communicated, and Beatrice’s immediate agreement makes the conversational act inferable.
